title: Positive earnings surprise on stock returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Event study with the market model.
- Approach: For each firm, estimate the market model ret_it = alpha_i + beta_i*mkt_ret_t + ε_it over the pre-event window [−10, −2]. Compute abnormal returns AR_it = ret_it − (alpha_i + beta_i*mkt_ret_t) during the event window [0, +2], then aggregate to CAR_i[0,+2] = sum_{t=0}^{2} AR_it. Test whether the cross-sectional mean CAR is greater than zero (t-test). Also report AAR by day and CAAR over the window.
- Key assumptions:
  - Correct model for normal returns: The market model fitted on [−10, −2] captures expected returns absent the event.
  - No confounding events in [0, +2] that systematically affect returns of these firms.
  - Event timing is exogenous to idiosyncratic shocks.
  - Cross-sectional independence (or weak dependence) so the standard t-test on the mean CAR is valid.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code that:
# - Reads the CSV file from the path provided
# - Runs the appropriate causal analysis
# - Prints a clear numerical result (coefficient, CAR, etc.)
# - Includes basic robustness checks

options(scipen = 99)

# 1) Load data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s14_data.csv"
dat <- read.csv(path)

# Basic checks
stopifnot(all(c("stock_id","event_day","ret","mkt_ret","beta") %in% names(dat)))

# Windows
est_window <- -10:-2
event_window <- 0:2
placebo_window <- -5:-1  # for a basic pre-event placebo check

# Helper: compute mean, t-stat, and two-sided p-value for a vector
summary_ttest <- function(x) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  n <- length(x)
  m <- mean(x)
  s <- sd(x)
  se <- s / sqrt(n)
  tstat <- m / se
  pval <- 2 * pt(-abs(tstat), df = n - 1)
  list(mean = m, t = tstat, p = pval, n = n)
}

# Containers
ids <- sort(unique(dat$stock_id))
N <- length(ids)

CAR_ols <- numeric(N)
CAR_beta_given <- numeric(N)
CAR_mar <- numeric(N)
CAR_placebo <- numeric(N)

# To compute AAR by event day for the primary spec
ar_records <- list()

# 2) Per-firm estimation and CAR computation
for (k in seq_along(ids)) {
  i <- ids[k]
  dfi <- dat[dat$stock_id == i, ]
  
  # Estimation and event samples
  est <- dfi[dfi$event_day %in% est_window, ]
  ev  <- dfi[dfi$event_day %in% event_window, ]
  pl  <- dfi[dfi$event_day %in% placebo_window, ]
  
  # Primary spec: OLS market model on [-10,-2]
  fit <- lm(ret ~ mkt_ret, data = est)
  co  <- coef(fit)
  alpha_hat <- as.numeric(co[1])
  beta_hat  <- as.numeric(co[2])
  
  # Abnormal returns in [0,+2]
  ev$AR_ols <- ev$ret - (alpha_hat + beta_hat * ev$mkt_ret)
  CAR_ols[k] <- sum(ev$AR_ols)
  
  # Store ARs for AAR/CAAR
  ar_records[[k]] <- data.frame(stock_id = i, event_day = ev$event_day, AR_ols = ev$AR_ols)
  
  # Robustness 1: Use provided beta, estimate alpha as mean(residual) on est window
  beta_given <- mean(est$beta)  # provided constant per firm
  alpha_given <- mean(est$ret - beta_given * est$mkt_ret)
  ev$AR_beta_given <- ev$ret - (alpha_given + beta_given * ev$mkt_ret)
  CAR_beta_given[k] <- sum(ev$AR_beta_given)
  
  # Robustness 2: Market-adjusted returns (alpha=0, beta=1)
  ev$AR_mar <- ev$ret - ev$mkt_ret
  CAR_mar[k] <- sum(ev$AR_mar)
  
  # Placebo CAR in [-5,-1] using OLS parameters
  if (nrow(pl) > 0) {
    pl$AR_pl <- pl$ret - (alpha_hat + beta_hat * pl$mkt_ret)
    CAR_placebo[k] <- sum(pl$AR_pl)
  } else {
    CAR_placebo[k] <- NA_real_
  }
}

# 3) Aggregate results for primary spec
primary <- summary_ttest(CAR_ols)
mean_CAR <- primary$mean
t_CAR    <- primary$t
p_CAR    <- primary$p
N_eff    <- primary$n

# AAR by event day and CAAR
ar_df <- do.call(rbind, ar_records)
AAR_by_day <- aggregate(AR_ols ~ event_day, data = ar_df, FUN = mean)
AAR_by_day <- AAR_by_day[order(AAR_by_day$event_day), ]
CAAR_0_2 <- sum(AAR_by_day$AR_ols[AAR_by_day$event_day %in% event_window])

# 4) Robustness summaries
rb1 <- summary_ttest(CAR_beta_given)
rb2 <- summary_ttest(CAR_mar)

# Sign test (one-sided: proportion of CAR > 0 greater than 0.5)
pos_count <- sum(CAR_ols > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
sign_test <- binom.test(pos_count, N_eff, p = 0.5, alternative = "greater")

# Placebo check on [-5,-1]
plc <- summary_ttest(CAR_placebo)

# 5) Print results
cat("Event Study: Positive earnings surprise, window [0,+2]\n")
cat(sprintf("N (firms) = %d\n\n", N_eff))

cat("Primary specification: Market model (OLS) estimated on [-10,-2]\n")
cat(sprintf("Mean CAR[0,+2] = %.3f%%, t = %.2f, p-value = %.4f\n",
            100 * mean_CAR, t_CAR, p_CAR))

cat("Daily AARs and CAAR (primary spec):\n")
for (d in event_window) {
  aar_d <- AAR_by_day$AR_ols[AAR_by_day$event_day == d]
  cat(sprintf("  AAR(day %d) = %.3f%%\n", d, 100 * aar_d))
}
cat(sprintf("  CAAR[0,+2] = %.3f%%\n\n", 100 * CAAR_0_2))

cat("Robustness checks:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Using provided beta (alpha re-estimated): Mean CAR = %.3f%%, t = %.2f, p = %.4f\n",
            100 * rb1$mean, rb1$t, rb1$p))
cat(sprintf("  Market-adjusted returns (beta=1, alpha=0): Mean CAR = %.3f%%, t = %.2f, p = %.4f\n",
            100 * rb2$mean, rb2$t, rb2$p))
cat(sprintf("  Sign test (CAR > 0): %d/%d positive, one-sided p = %.4f\n\n",
            pos_count, N_eff, sign_test$p.value))

cat("Placebo (pre-event) check using [-5,-1] with OLS parameters:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Mean placebo CAR[-5,-1] = %.3f%%, t = %.2f, p = %.4f\n",
            100 * plc$mean, plc$t, plc$p))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. Firms with positive earnings surprises typically earn positive abnormal returns on and shortly after the announcement.
- Magnitude: I expect CAAR[0,+2] around +0.8% to +2.0%, with day 0 AAR positive and the bulk of the effect on day 0 or 1. Given 80 firms, the mean CAR should be statistically significant at conventional levels. Robustness checks (provided beta; market-adjusted) should yield similar positive results, and the sign test should show a majority of firms with CAR > 0.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Event study — market model; positive surprise sample; event window [0,+2]
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Firms with positive earnings surprises earn significantly positive CAR
